session_covered: US and European sessions of Wednesday 14 October
intro: Covers the Wednesday 14 October US session (Europe closed higher). Several closing prints could not be sourced from primary closing reports; index and commodity levels are largely CFD-based reference prices (Trading Economics) and are footnoted where approximate. SPI 200 futures sources conflicted and are marked not available.
footnotes: NASDAQ Composite: the email gave "not available not available (c. -2% intraday)1", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.
VIX: approximate figure (the email gave "c. 17.1 pts c. +12%2").
AUD/USD: approximate figure (the email gave "US$0.698 c. -0.1%4").

NASDAQ Composite: Composite close not found in any closing report; Nasdaq 100 closed -2.14% (Trading Economics) and the Composite was down about 1.9-2.1% in late-session reports (prior close 27,204.38).
VIX: Yahoo Finance 17.07 (+11.8%) late session; Trading Economics 17.18.
US 10-year Treasury yield: Trading Economics and Investing.com agree on 5.19%/-3 bp at the close; the yield reached about 5.32% intraday.
AUD/USD: Trading Economics shows -0.12% (stats) vs 0% (widget); the AUD touched about US$0.70 earlier.
Brent crude: Trading Economics +0.3%; AP reported +1% to US$106.71 in the afternoon.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures: not available. Sources conflict on direction (TradingView -0.34% at 8,717 in one field and +0.14% on the October contract in another; Investing.com +0.78% on a stale-looking December print), so no implied open is stated. The US risk-off tone is consistent with a weaker open, but that is not a quantified estimate. Prior ASX 200 close (Wednesday): about 8,674, roughly -1.3% from Tuesday's 8,784 (Trading Economics; its headline -0.64% does not reconcile with the levels).

local_events: ABS labour force data for September (August unemployment was 4.6%, the highest since late 2021).
Markets price about a 28% chance of an RBA hike on 3 November and about 50% by December.
what_moved: A hotter-than-expected September US CPI (3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected; core 2.6%) lifted odds of another Fed rate hike and hit long-duration tech. Technology led declines (about -2.6% to -2.7% midday) with communication services about -1.8%; health care (about +2%) was the main advancer. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell almost 4%, its sixth straight loss. Gold fell below US$4,100 on the rate-hike repricing. Sector figures are intraday readings; closes not found.

news.headline: US CPI runs hot.
news.summary: September consumer prices rose 3.7% y/y (3.4% in August), driven by fuel costs tied to the Iran conflict; monthly CPI was 0.6%.

news.headline: Fed hike odds jump.
news.summary: Traders priced roughly 37-47% odds of a rate rise at the next Fed meeting (about two weeks away), up from 22% a day earlier; estimates vary by source.

news.headline: Long yields near 2002 highs.
news.summary: The US 10-year briefly topped 5.32% intraday before easing to about 5.19% at the close.

news.headline: AI and chip sell-off deepens.
news.summary: Semiconductors extended losses after a roughly 12% five-day fall in South Korea's KOSPI; AI-infrastructure names fell sharply (Oracle -7.3%, CoreWeave -15% intraday).

news.headline: Bank of America miss weighs on financials.
news.summary: Q3 profit fell 17% on a US$1.2 billion regulatory charge; the stock fell about 6%, as did State Street after weaker results.

news.headline: Brent holds near US$106.
news.summary: Hormuz export flows improved but Houthi strikes on Saudi targets and tanker attacks keep supply risk elevated; Brent is up about 71% y/y.

news.headline: ASX 200 slid on Wednesday.
news.summary: Financials, consumer durables and transport led losses; the big four banks fell 0.9-2.3% ahead of today's jobs data.

news.headline: Iron ore steady, gold lower.
news.summary: Iron ore is about 7% lower over the past month at US$90.74/t; gold hit its lowest since early August.

news.headline: AUD near US$0.70.
news.summary: The currency reached a two-week high on hawkish RBA signals and a softer US dollar.

coming_up: Today (15 October): Australian labour force data; TSMC earnings (US time). Next: the Fed meeting in about two weeks (exact date not verified), Australian Q3 CPI later this month, and the RBA decision on 3 November.
